A1.justification: Both complete 15-page PDFs describe ZigzagPointMamba and include Appendix A.1–A.2. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that pages 2–15 are identical; differences are confined to the first page.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, few-shot learning, segmentation and ablation results in Section 4, plus reconstruction and segmentation examples in Appendix A.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and the qualitative reconstruction and segmentation results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical zigzag scanning, token construction, Semantic-Siamese Masking followed by random masking, and Mamba autoencoder procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ModelNet40 classification and few-shot tasks, three ScanObjectNN scenarios, ShapeNetPart segmentation, and ShapeNet validation reconstruction examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within Tables 1–4, including PointMamba and the table-specific ReCon and PointGPT-S comparisons. Tables 6–7 also retain the same attention and scanning alternatives.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains identical model sizes, input resolution, masking settings, 300-epoch pre-training, ModelNet40 evaluation without voting, and few-shot sampling procedures.

E4.justification: The SMS-threshold, attention-mechanism and scanning-curve analyses in Tables 5–7 are unchanged. Figure 1 and Appendix A retain the same feature, reconstruction and segmentation analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 15 independent few-shot experiments and identical ± reporting in Table 4. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results match. For example, both report 93.15% ModelNet40 accuracy in Table 2 and 85.78% instance mIoU and 84.16% class mIoU in Table 3.

T1.justification: The state-space equations, scanning-layer definitions, similarity and redundancy calculations, and masking formulas in Section 3 are identical. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and performance claims concerning zigzag spatial continuity, SMS semantic modeling and downstream improvements.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of redundancy and over-masking, the claimed synergy between scanning and SMS, and the qualification that zigzag scanning alone is not outstanding in Table 7.

D1.justification: v1’s abstract supplies a code-availability statement and repository hyperlink; v5 removes both without a replacement. Implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain identical. This establishes removal of access guidance, not withdrawal of the external repository.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, all 42 references, and the positioning relative to PointMamba, Transformer methods and earlier scanning approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: First-page edits remove the code sentence, replace the NeurIPS 2025 footer with “Preprint,” and update the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, section organization and appendices remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6, Tables 1–7, captions, legends and placement are identical. The first-page text substitutions and deletion preserve the page arrangement; the remaining rendered pages match exactly.

improvement.justification: v5 removes the sole code-access statement and hyperlink without replacing them, reducing the document’s reproducibility guidance. The scientific content and supporting evidence, including the appendices, are unchanged. This is a limited documentary deterioration; the PDFs do not establish whether the repository itself remains available.
